reason: The text demonstrates that individuals without formal leadership authority exercise significant agency. Moses, not yet established as a leader, independently observes his people's suffering, identifies an injustice, kills the Egyptian taskmaster, and conceals the body—all acts of agency undertaken without any position of authority. Similarly, the Hebrew men fighting, the Egyptian striking, and even Pharaoh responding to events all exercise agency regardless of formal leadership status. The text directly contradicts the statement by showing that moral agency and decisive action originate from individuals across all social strata, not exclusively from those in positions of power.
